name: Brown Gravy Soup
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: onions, if small button onions—one, if large
ingredients.originalText: 6 onions, if small button onions—one, if large

ingredients.name: glass of pale Sherry
ingredients.originalText: half a glass of pale Sherry

instructions.text: Have ready some nice dripping in a frying-pan.
Slice the onions and fry them brown.
Take them out and set them by in a covered pan to keep warm.
Cut the beef into bits an inch long and half an inch thick, and fry them brown also, turning frequently lest they should burn.
Chop the vegetables and put them with the meat and onions into a covered pot.
Pour on the water and let all stew together for two hours.
Throw in salt and pepper and boil one hour longer, skimming very carefully.
Strain; put back over the fire; boil up once more to make the liquid perfectly clear, skim.
Add a handful of vermicelli that has been boiled separately and drained dry, or put in the vermicelli after the soup is poured into the tureen.
Do not stir before it goes to table.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Have ready some nice dripping in a frying-pan.
2. Slice the onions and fry them brown.
3. Take them out and set them by in a covered pan to keep warm.
4. Cut the beef into bits an inch long and half an inch thick, and fry them brown also, turning frequently lest they should burn.
5. Chop the vegetables and put them with the meat and onions into a covered pot.
6. Pour on the water and let all stew together for two hours.
7. Throw in salt and pepper and boil one hour longer, skimming very carefully.
8. Strain; put back over the fire; boil up once more to make the liquid perfectly clear, skim.
9. Add a handful of vermicelli that has been boiled separately and drained dry, or put in the vermicelli after the soup is poured into the tureen.
10. Do not stir before it goes to table.
